findings.summary: Requiring an active Connection before a goal can be saved contradicts the Purpose constraint and the private-contacts feature, which say the app must help before any friend installs it and that goals are owner-only and independent of connecting accounts.
findings.evidence: Diff: "A goal may be saved only for a contact with an active Connection." vs purpose.yaml constraints: "The app can help before any friend installs it." and "connecting accounts adds consensual sharing capabilities and does not turn private notes or goals into shared data"; GD.contacts: "Keep a private contact record before any friend installs the app"

findings.summary: Goal saving now depends on entity.Connection, but evolution.2 (goals) is scheduled before evolution.3, which introduces Connection, so the goals evolution cannot satisfy its own precondition.
findings.evidence: operation.goal.save links: "{ rel: reads, to: entity.Connection }"; evolution.3 affectedNodes includes entity.Connection and "dependsOn: evolution.2"; evolution.2 affects operation.goal.save

findings.summary: Snooze, pause and revise on Today all go through operation.goal.save, so after a Disconnect the owner can no longer snooze, pause or revise an existing goal, even though Disconnect is meant to keep private records under the owner's control.
findings.evidence: J.prompts p5/p6/p7 operation: operation.goal.save; new failure "A goal for an unconnected contact is refused"; ConnectionPanel.disconnect effects: "private records remain under the owner's control"
